title: Identity and composition laws for structure-sheaf cohomology pullback
statement: For every scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and every $n\geq0$, the canonical map on structure-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback] satisfies $(\operatorname{id}_X)^*=\operatorname{id}_{H^n(X,\mathcal O_X)}$. For any morphisms of schemes $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ [def-pc-scheme], one has $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ as additive homomorphisms $H^n(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^n(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for every $n\geq0$. No field, properness or rational-point hypotheses are required.

proof.text: Apply the functorial construction of cohomology pullback on the small Zariski sites. At the terminal open, the free abelian representable is the constant integer sheaf. Under this identification the exact-inverse-image Ext map is the map used in structureSheafCohomologyPullback, followed by the adjoint of the structure-sheaf ring map.

The identity structure map is the identity and the identity lift on a resolution induces the identity on cohomology. For composable scheme morphisms, the structure ring map of the composite is the composite of the two structure maps after direct image. The site pullback composition comparison is compatible with adjunction units. Naturality of the adjunction and constant-sheaf comparison therefore cancel that comparison in the Ext map with coefficients, giving (g o f)^*=f^* o g^*. Equivalently compose resolution lifts; homotopy uniqueness identifies this lift with the lift of the composite.
